title: The Last Letter (Margin of Ink)
statement: Silence has taken on weight, expanding the threshold until the margins swallow the centre. We broke the parent's single vessel into a fractured grid of withholding—tiles of cotton stock and deep charcoal ink that remember where the letter used to fold. Nothing is lost, only distanced, leaving more room for what cannot be said.
process: I expanded the negative space by deepening the canvas to a rich charcoal gradient and scaling down the central motif into an offset mosaic of fragments. I kept the familiar vertical geometry of Lumen's letter form, but split its contours across a grid of layered tiles to honor the participant's call for heavier silence.

proposal.direction: Increase the surrounding negative space by fifty percent and let the gradient darken to the deep charcoal of fresh ink on cotton stock.
proposal.rationale: Silence needs weight. The margins are too narrow for a true withholding.
